pages.text: How to Access Your Taboola Data English Taboola’s Data Subject Access Request Portal This policy outlines what personal data and behavioural information Taboola holds about you and how you can access or delete your personal data. Your Rights — What You Can Request You have the right to request that Taboola provide you with access to the personal data that we hold about you, correct your personal data, delete your personal data, and cease or restrict processing of your personal data. You have also the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection authority about our collection and use of your Personal Data, including the UK Information Commissioner's Office where applicable. However, if you have any questions or concerns about our collection and use of your Personal Data, including any complaints, please first contact us at privacy@taboola.com so we can review and address them. If you are unable to obtain the information or resolution that you seek, you may also contact our Data Protection Officer at dpo@taboola.com. To learn more, please contact your local data protection authority, via the contact methods available here. For more information about how we collect, use, and disclose information that we obtain through our websites and services, please see our Privacy Policy. What Information Taboola Holds Taboola maintains data about you in only pseudonymized form, which means that we do not know your identity because we do not process your name, email address, or other identifiable data. Instead, we only process digital identifiers such as cookie IDs, IP addresses (truncated in Germany), mobile advertising IDs on your device, and in some limited circumstances, your hashed email address (for a full list of pseudonymized data that we process, please see our Privacy Policy). pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Centeda.com
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Centeda.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name centeda.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including centeda.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Informat

Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name centeda.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including centeda.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Informat

pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Dataveria.com
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Dataveria.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name dataveria.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including dataveria.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected In

pages.title: National Do Not Call Registry
pages.text: Back to ftc.gov | Español Resources | Privacy Act Statement | Home The National Do Not Call Registry gives you a choice about whether to receive telemarketing calls You can register your home or mobile phone for free. After you register, other types of organizations may still call you, such as charities, political groups, debt collectors and surveys. To learn more, read our FAQs. If you received an unwanted call after your number was on the National Registry for 31 days, report it to the FTC. Sellers and telemarketers: Go to https://telemarketing.donotcall.gov to access the National Do Not Call Registry. Back to ftc.gov | Privacy Policy

pages.title: Delete vital information from Family Tree • FamilySearch
pages.text: How do I remove Vitals information in Family Tree? Article Id: 1288 August 05, 2025 SHARE Print You can delete vital information from an individual's profile, even if you are not the original contributor. You cannot delete some information: Name Sex Death information (unless you first change the status of the person to Living) Steps (website) Sign in to FamilySearch, click Family Tree, and then click Tree. Find the person that you want to edit. Click the person's name. In the details that pop up, click the person's name again. Click the Details tab. Under Vitals, find the information that you want to delete. Click the Edit icon. Review the current information and any reason statements. On the left side of the edit box, click Delete. If the box lacks a Delete option, you can only edit the information. Explain why you made a change. Click Delete. Steps (mobile app) In the Family Tree mobile app, navigate to the Person page that you want to edit. Tap the Details tab. Under Vitals, tap the information you want to delete. Review the current information and any reason statements. Tap Delete. If you do not see the Delete option, you can only edit the information. Explain why you made a change. Tap Delete. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Mercer County Docket No. MER-L-000286-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name golookup.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Lucky2Media, LLC, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 18,882 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 25, 2025 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Lucky2Media, LLC. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendant violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Lucky2Media, LLC and all persons acting in concert with it are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation through: golookup.com (the ‘Domain Name’) as well as any subdomains, affiliated domains or sites w

pages.text: Privacy Requests Two different things you can do here. Pick the one you want — they work differently, and only one of them takes a record off the site. What would you like to do? Your Privacy Choices Stop us selling or sharing your information, and limit how we use sensitive personal information. Takes effect straight away — no account, no identity check, nothing to confirm afterwards. This does not remove a listing. Remove My Information Stops results for a person being returned — from new searches, from reports our members already have, and from matching records we take in later. Needs enough detail to identify the right person, and one confirmation click. Your Privacy Choices Press submit and we will stop disclosing your information to third parties for their own purposes, including advertising partners and referral affiliates, and will use sensitive personal information only for the limited purposes the law permits. We'll still use your information to run this site and to provide what you ask for. Tell us who to record it for Give an email address or a phone number — either one is enough. That is what your choice is recorded against, so it applies on your other devices and to any account you have with us. We don't ask you to prove it is yours. Email Phone 10 digits, digits only — leave out the leading 1. Submit What happens next Your choice is recorded the moment you submit. We apply it everywhere else within 15 business days. You'll see a confirmation on the next screen — there's nothing else to do, and we won't email you a link to click. Browser privacy signals If your browser or an extension sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request not to sell or share your personal information and apply it automatically. You don't need to use this page as well, though you can. How we use what you enter Anything you enter here is used only to process this request. pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Newenglandfacts.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name newenglandfacts.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including newenglandfacts.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Per

pages.text: Home Privacy Policy Contact Us Privacy policy Last updated: Jan 6, 2025 Introduction Online Media Group is a management company overseeing a suite of innovative products designed to help businesses develop world-class, data-enabled solutions. Our partners utilize these products to enhance decision-making in private and public equity investments, identify promising sales opportunities in high-growth markets, recruit top-tier talent, and more. Our focus remains on providing actionable insights primarily concerning companies and their current and prospective employees. Booking data, court case files, active warrants, and jail rosters are held by 88 separate county systems — each Sheriff’s office and Clerk of Courts operates its own database, on its own schedule, under its own interface. Statewide portals exist for court records and state prison custody, but they cover different slices of the picture. This site maps all of those systems, names the right official source for each record type, and routes you directly to it. What you can look up here Three types of records bring most people to this site. Arrest records are booking logs created when a person is taken into custody at a county jail. They typically include the person’s name, date of birth, the charges listed at booking, and the arresting agency. These records live with the county Sheriff or the local jail, not with any statewide arrest database. The county pages in the index below link directly to each county’s official booking roster. pages.title: Domain Update — PeekYou.com
pages.text: Domain Update — PeekYou.com Domain Update Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. PeekYou LLC, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Essex County Docket No. ESX-L-003299-25 The domain name peekyou.com is now controlled by Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”). On April 30, 2025 , Atlas and three individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. PeekYou LLC, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,700 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. Atlas and PeekYou LLC have entered into a settlement agreement, and this lawsuit has now been resolved. Additional information regarding this and other Daniel’s Law cases can be obtained from the Superior Court of New Jersey. pages.text: People Search Reverse Phone Lookup Free People Search & Public Records Search by name, address or phone number to find public records, relatives and contact details. Search Now What Information Can a People Search Reveal? Aliases Age Location History Previous Addresses Phone Number(s) Family Members How to Search Public Records Online for Free People-Search.org gives you instant access to billions of public records collected from government agencies, courthouses, and official registries across all 50 states. Enter a full name or phone number to begin your lookup — no registration or payment required. You might be surprised by how much personal information exists in publicly accessible databases. Government agencies routinely publish records related to property ownership, voter registration, court filings, and vital statistics. Under federal and state transparency laws, much of this data is available to any member of the public. The types of records you can uncover through a people search include: Current and previous addresses — residential history sourced from public filings and utility records Phone numbers and email contacts — including landlines, mobile numbers, and associated accounts Relatives and associates — household members, family connections, and known associates Age, date of birth, and aliases — identity details drawn from vital records and official documents Arrest and criminal records — court filings, bookings, and offense history from county, state, and federal sources Marriage and divorce records — certificates filed with county clerks and state vital records offices Sex offender registry status — listings from the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) and state registries All of this information comes from publicly available sources. People-Search.org aggregates these records into a single, easy-to-read report — saving you the time and effort of searching dozens of individual databases on your own. pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — TelephoneDirectories.us This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. TelephoneDirectories.US, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Mercer County Docket No. MER-L-000335-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name telephonedirectories.us has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 15, 2024 , Atlas and eight individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. TelephoneDirectories.US, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 19,052 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On November 14, 2025 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against TelephoneDirectories.US. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendant violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that TelephoneDirectories.US and all persons acting in concert with it are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation through: TelephoneDirectories.US (the ‘Dom

Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name pub360.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including pub360.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information

pages.text: Privacy Requests Two different things you can do here. Pick the one you want — they work differently, and only one of them takes a record off the site. What would you like to do? Your Privacy Choices Stop us selling or sharing your information, and limit how we use sensitive personal information. Takes effect straight away — no account, no identity check, nothing to confirm afterwards. This does not remove a listing. Remove My Information Stops results for a person being returned — from new searches, from reports our members already have, and from matching records we take in later. Needs enough detail to identify the right person, and one confirmation click. Your Privacy Choices Press submit and we will stop disclosing your information to third parties for their own purposes, including advertising partners and referral affiliates, and will use sensitive personal information only for the limited purposes the law permits. We'll still use your information to run this site and to provide what you ask for. Tell us who to record it for Give an email address or a phone number — either one is enough. That is what your choice is recorded against, so it applies on your other devices and to any account you have with us. We don't ask you to prove it is yours. Email Phone 10 digits, digits only — leave out the leading 1. Submit What happens next Your choice is recorded the moment you submit. We apply it everywhere else within 15 business days. You'll see a confirmation on the next screen — there's nothing else to do, and we won't email you a link to click. Browser privacy signals If your browser or an extension sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request not to sell or share your personal information and apply it automatically. You don't need to use this page as well, though you can. How we use what you enter Anything you enter here is used only to process this request. It's never added to our listings, and is never sold or shared. Authorized agents An author

pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Rain-street.org This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name rain-street.org has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including rain-street.org. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protec

pages.text: $ SBA Loan Data Borrowers Lenders Franchises Industries States Rankings Loan Calculator Home / Privacy Privacy & Removal Requests Where this information comes from Everything on SBA Loan Data comes from loan records the SBA publishes itself under the Freedom of Information Act. We do not collect, buy, or infer any information beyond what is in those files. The SBA withholds sensitive loan detail under FOIA Exemption 4 before publication. Sole proprietors and personal names Some SBA borrowers are sole proprietors recorded under a personal name rather than a business name. Where a borrower name appears to belong to a private individual, we deliberately do not create a search-indexable page for it: those records carry a noindex directive and are left out of our sitemap, so they do not surface in search engines. The underlying record remains part of the public dataset either way. A note on charged-off loans “Charged off” is the SBA's accounting status for a loan whose remaining balance was written off. It is not a finding of fraud, wrongdoing, or bankruptcy, and many businesses with a charged-off loan are still trading. We label it neutrally and show the SBA's own definition wherever it appears. Corrections and removals If a page is factually wrong — a loan attributed to the wrong business, two businesses merged into one record, or a name that belongs to a private individual — write to removals@sbaloandata.org with the page URL and what is incorrect. We will correct or suppress the page. We cannot change the SBA's source data. To correct the underlying record, contact the SBA directly; our next quarterly refresh will pick up the change. Analytics This is a static site. We set no advertising or tracking cookies and run no third-party analytics scripts. Aggregate traffic statistics come from our CDN and are not tied to individual visitors. SBA Loan Data Every SBA 7(a) and 504 loan approved since 1991, free and searchable. pages.text: Privacy Requests Two different things you can do here. Pick the one you want — they work differently, and only one of them takes a record off the site. What would you like to do? Your Privacy Choices Stop us selling or sharing your information, and limit how we use sensitive personal information. Takes effect straight away — no account, no identity check, nothing to confirm afterwards. This does not remove a listing. Remove My Information Stops results for a person being returned — from new searches, from reports our members already have, and from matching records we take in later. Needs enough detail to identify the right person, and one confirmation click. Your Privacy Choices Press submit and we will stop disclosing your information to third parties for their own purposes, including advertising partners and referral affiliates, and will use sensitive personal information only for the limited purposes the law permits. We'll still use your information to run this site and to provide what you ask for. Tell us who to record it for Give an email address or a phone number — either one is enough. That is what your choice is recorded against, so it applies on your other devices and to any account you have with us. We don't ask you to prove it is yours. Email Phone 10 digits, digits only — leave out the leading 1. Submit What happens next Your choice is recorded the moment you submit. We apply it everywhere else within 15 business days. You'll see a confirmation on the next screen — there's nothing else to do, and we won't email you a link to click. Browser privacy signals If your browser or an extension sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request not to sell or share your personal information and apply it automatically. pages.text: Privacy Requests Two different things you can do here. Pick the one you want — they work differently, and only one of them takes a record off the site. What would you like to do? Your Privacy Choices Stop us selling or sharing your information, and limit how we use sensitive personal information. Takes effect straight away — no account, no identity check, nothing to confirm afterwards. This does not remove a listing. Remove My Information Stops results for a person being returned — from new searches, from reports our members already have, and from matching records we take in later. Needs enough detail to identify the right person, and one confirmation click. Your Privacy Choices Press submit and we will stop disclosing your information to third parties for their own purposes, including advertising partners and referral affiliates, and will use sensitive personal information only for the limited purposes the law permits. We'll still use your information to run this site and to provide what you ask for. Tell us who to record it for Give an email address or a phone number — either one is enough. That is what your choice is recorded against, so it applies on your other devices and to any account you have with us. We don't ask you to prove it is yours. Email Phone 10 digits, digits only — leave out the leading 1. Submit What happens next Your choice is recorded the moment you submit. We apply it everywhere else within 15 business days. You'll see a confirmation on the next screen — there's nothing else to do, and we won't email you a link to click. Browser privacy signals If your browser or an extension sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request not to sell or share your personal information and apply it automatically. pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Verecor.com
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Verecor.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name verecor.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including verecor.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Informat

Information Collection and Use For a better experience while using our Service, we may require you to provide us with certain personally identifiable information, including but not limited to your name, phone number, and postal address. The information that we collect will be used to contact or identify you. Log Data We want to inform you that whenever you visit our Service, we collect information that your browser sends to us that is called Log Data. pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Rain-street.org
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Rain-street.org This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name rain-street.org has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including rain-street.org. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protec

pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Centeda.com
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Centeda.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name centeda.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including centeda.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Informat

pages.text: Skip to Main Content Resources Industries Solutions Company Contact Us Circana Insights Circana Completes Acquisition of NCSolutions By Circana Jun 2, 2025 We are thrilled to welcome the talented NCS team to Circana and meaningfully enhance our media capabilities. Allocating finite marketing resources is one of the most critical and challenging decisions organizations face today – and there is no substitute for comprehensive, real-time data and actionable insights to optimize outcomes. Est. Read Time: 3 mins You're reading: Circana Completes Acquisition of NCSolutions Like it? Share it! CHICAGO and NEW YORK — June 2, 2025 — Circana, LLC has announced the successful completion of its acquisition of NCSolutions (NCS), the joint venture between Nielsen and Catalina that improves advertising effectiveness. With this acquisition, Circana significantly expands its media measurement capabilities. Circana announced its intent to acquire NCS last year. “We are thrilled to welcome the talented NCS team to Circana and meaningfully enhance our media capabilities,” said Stuart Aitken, president and chief executive officer of Circana. “Allocating finite marketing resources is one of the most critical and challenging decisions organizations face today – and there is no substitute for comprehensive, real-time data and actionable insights to optimize outcomes. Bringing together Circana and NCS data, technology assets, and industry-leading expertise will deliver more value for our clients as we work with them to maximize every media and marketing dollar they spend.” Clients of both organizations will gain broader access to audience targeting, media measurement, in-flight optimization, and clean room solutions. This combination will also increase efficiency and offer improved products and services to fuel clients’ growth through more targeted and impactful advertising. pages.title: Circana Privacy Web Form
pages.text: Do Not Sell My Information Many consumers enjoy seeing advertisements that relate to their own interests and shopping habits. Tailored advertisements have many benefits: they help consumers find products they might not have otherwise discovered, they highlight promotions and deals on much loved products and they reduce the annoyance of seeing irrelevant content. While Circana does not serve personalized advertising directly, through our Audience segments we help our clients identify which advertisements should be served to which US households. As leading experts in consumer behavior, we also appreciate the importance of privacy to consumers. Therefore we have developed a privacy safe model that means we do not receive or sell directly identifying information (such as name, surname, address or email address etc) on any US citizen. Instead we use identity numbers to process data at a household level only. You have choices Consumers in all US states may learn more about online advertising and opt out of interest-based advertising from online advertising companies that are also members of applicable self-regulatory organizations by visiting their opt-out links below. Your device may be scanned to determine what cookies are stored on your machine. You may select the companies that maintain those cookies and opt out of all their individual advertising or all targeted advertising in general. Network Advertising Initiative (NAI) – http://optout.networkadvertising.org/ Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) – http://optout.aboutads.info/ DAA AppChoices page – http://www.aboutads.info/appchoices In addition, you may follow the instructions provided for your mobile device or in your internet browser’s help file to change privacy, advertising and tracking settings. Additionally consumers in California and Oregon can request that we do not sell to our customers the household identifier that we process. pages.text: Privacy Policy – Drunk Drivers Skip to content Drunk Drivers Driving under the influence is a serious crime with serious crime with serious consequences Menu DISCLAIMER Privacy Policy Submit a story Stories Drunk Driving Offenders Remove My Info Privacy Policy Spread the love Who we are Suggested text: Our website address is: https://drunkdrivers.org. Comments Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection. Product AgentSource® MCP Server API Documentation Data Our Data Data Affiliation Use Cases Sales GTM Engineering Marketing Recruiting Integrations Pricing Company About Explorium Resource Center Blog Careers Contact Us Get a Demo | Login Sign Up Back to Blog What SLA Terms Should You Look for in a B2B Data API Contract? Explorium Team · Business Data · Oct 04, 2026 · 14 min read Table of Content ▾ TL;DR Score any B2B data API contract against 8 non-negotiable SLA categories before signing, or your production agents run unprotected. 99.9% uptime permits 43 minutes of monthly downtime, but maintenance exclusions and partial degradation loopholes often make effective availability far worse. Demand percentile-based latency SLAs (P50 ≤500ms, P95 ≤2s), QPM ≥200 with burst allowance, and contractual data-quality guarantees including match rate and field-fill rate. Service credits rarely exceed 10–25% of monthly fees, covering a fraction of the $50K+ downstream pipeline damage from misrouted leads during outage windows. Multi-source aggregation architecture, like Explorium's 50+ provider layer, structurally prevents single-point-of-failure downtime that voids single-source vendor SLAs. Use the 10-point SLA readiness scorecard to rate any vendor in 5 minutes; production-ready vendors score 16–20 across uptime, latency, QPM, credits, data quality, and support. Q1. What SLA Terms Should You Look for in a B2B Data API Contract? Use this Explorium checklist to score any B2B data API vendor contract against these 8 SLA categories before you sign. pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — GoLookup.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Lucky2Media, LLC, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Mercer County Docket No. MER-L-000286-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name golookup.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Lucky2Media, LLC, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 18,882 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 25, 2025 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Lucky2Media, LLC. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendant violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Lucky2Media, LLC and all persons acting in concert with it are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation through: golookup.com (the ‘Domain Name’) as well as any subdomains, affiliated domains or sites w

pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Newenglandfacts.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name newenglandfacts.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including newenglandfacts.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Per

pages.text: Domain Update — RevealName.com Domain Update Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Revealname.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000901-24 The domain name revealname.com is now controlled by Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”). On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and seven individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Revealname.com, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 18,996 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. Atlas and the operator of the Revealname.com website have entered into a settlement agreement, and this lawsuit has now been resolved. Additional information regarding this and other Daniel’s Law cases can be obtained from the Superior Court of New Jersey. pages.title: Legal Relationship with the Child
pages.text: Legal Relationship with the Child Legal Relationship with the Child How to Legally Care for a Child Section 1: Family-planned or Arranged Care Section 2: Power of Attorney for Care of a Minor Child Section 3: Legal Custody Section 4: Kinship Foster Care Section 5: Permanent Guardianship Section 6: Adoption Q. What are the legal options for relative caregivers? A. Currently, there are six ways to legally care for the child you are related to. Scroll down on this page to see the six sections, or click the links on the right to jump to a section. View Chart of Legal Options for Relative Caregivers Section 1: Family-planned or Arranged Care This is probably the most common kinship care arrangement. This type of care is also referred to as physical placement, physical custody or informal care. This is when a parent asks you to take care of the child or leaves the child with you to take care of full-time. The child lives with you, and you take care of the child's daily needs. However, the parent does not sign any legal papers. The court is not involved. The Department of Children's Services (DCS) is not involved. With this option, you don't have legal custody. Although your decision-making power might never be challenged, your legal authority to make major decisions for the child is very limited. With family-planned care, either parent can take back the child whenever he or she wants. You may have problems enrolling the child in school or daycare. You may be able to get simple medical care. However, you can't make major medical decisions. Sometimes medical providers and schools will only give information to a person who has written proof of having a legal relationship. Other times there is an emergency and the child's parent can't be reached, or the parents are unable or unwilling to help. pages.title: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Verecor.com
pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Verecor.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name verecor.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including verecor.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. §§ 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and all persons acting in concert with them are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Informat

In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On June 12, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Radaris, LLC, Radaris America, Inc., and twelve domain-name defendants, including veriforia.com. pages.text: Domain Update — PeekYou.com Domain Update Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. PeekYou LLC, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Essex County Docket No. ESX-L-003299-25 The domain name peekyou.com is now controlled by Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”). On April 30, 2025 , Atlas and three individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. PeekYou LLC, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,700 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. Atlas and PeekYou LLC have entered into a settlement agreement, and this lawsuit has now been resolved. pages.text: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — TelephoneDirectories.us This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. TelephoneDirectories.US, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Mercer County Docket No. MER-L-000335-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name telephonedirectories.us has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 15, 2024 , Atlas and eight individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. TelephoneDirectories.US, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 19,052 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On November 14, 2025 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against TelephoneDirectories.US. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendant violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that TelephoneDirectories.US and all persons acting in concert with it are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation through: TelephoneDirectories.US (the ‘Dom

Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name radaris.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On August 27, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Defendants Radaris.com, Rehold.com, and Trustoria.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and “all persons in concert” with Defendants are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation thro

pages.text: Data Privacy Center Take control of your user and public data. User Data Tools User Data is personal information or personal data as defined by applicable state data privacy laws, such as the CCPA, and primarily consists of identifying data that we collect directly from you when you interact with our site as a visitor or customer including your email address, search history, payment records, etc. The definition of personal information and personal data under these laws does not include publicly available information. To exercise options we provide with respect to that information, please see our Public Data tools. Subject to applicable state data privacy laws, Intelius allows all users to exercise the following rights to User Data: Right to Know Right to Opt Out Right to Correct Right to Delete View User Data Tools Right to Know You can receive a report of the User Data we hold about you, such as your email address, search history or payment records, free of charge. If you are a customer, you will be prompted to login to submit your request. You will be sent a link by email to download your User Data. It will be available for 72 hours from completion, after which it is automatically purged for your privacy. If you do not have access to the email address you provided when interacting with our website, you may email us at privacy@intelius.com. We will require you to verify your identity prior to processing your request, and may deny your request if we cannot verify your identity. Residents of Connecticut, Minnesota, and Oregon have rights to receive additional information relating to the third parties with whom we have shared personal information. To request that information, please email us here and confirm you are a resident of Connecticut, Minnesota, or Oregon and are seeking to exercise this right. Comments When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection. An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment. Media If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website. Cookies If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year. If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser. When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select “Remember Me”, your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed. If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. pages.title: Privacy Policy - Street Directory
pages.text: Privacy Policy - Street Directory Skip to content Street Directory Home About us Privacy Policy Privacy Policy Who we are Our website address is: https://streetdirectory.com.my. Comments When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection. An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment. Media If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website. Cookies If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year. If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser. When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select “Remember Me”, your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed. If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. pages.title: Your Privacy - USATrace.com
pages.text: Skip to content Home > Your Privacy Your Privacy Your Digital Footprint In the digital world we live in, we are constantly interacting with companies and entities which create and leave behind a digital footprint. Though we don’t always realize it, many of these records are publicly available and, in many cases, this is because of state laws or the terms and conditions of websites and apps that we interact with. This information is gathered and indexed to create profiles of almost everyone in the United States and the companies that combine this information together are known as data brokers. Data Brokers Some data brokers make this information for legal professionals, law enforcement, employers, and lenders while others make public information easily accessible to the public. Background checks and credit checks are used every day – very often through data brokers – to assist in official decision making for employment and credit decisions. In addition, millions of people have used publicly available people search tools for useful purposes like reconnecting with old friends and loved ones and validating new relationships. USA Trace was developed by private investigators and legal professionals who have used data brokers for official purposes as part of our professions. We understand where to find information and the types of information available. However, USA Trace is not a data broker – we do not store any information, nor do we have access to the information contained in the public record profiles. USA Trace has instead partnered with data brokers and created different ways to find these profiles. One of the ways we do this is with the search results seen on USA Trace, which are previews of the full data available with our partners. However, we don’t even store this incomplete preview information. If you would like to opt out of the sharing of your Personal Information collected from this website or application for this purpose, please click this button: DO NOT SELL OR SHARE MY PERSONAL INFORMATION The functionality of this button relies on browser cookies to store your opt-out preferences. If you subsequently clear or delete your browser's cookies, you will have to click this button again to update your preferences. If the "DO NOT SELL OR SHARE MY PERSONAL INFORMATION" button is not active for this site or application, either you have already opted-out or we do not sell or share personal information collected about you here.
